title: Floriculture and landscaping
competency: Explain the concept of floriculture and its opportunities and importance in Ethiopia.

keywords.def: The branch of horticulture that grows flowering and decorative plants and includes landscape gardening; ornamental horticulture.
A plant, or plant part, that is decorative, showy and attractive, used for beauty and function.

en.text: Floriculture, also called ornamental horticulture, is the branch of horticulture that grows flowering plants, decorative foliage plants, cacti, orchids, succulents, bonsai, ferns and container plants, and includes landscape gardening. Ornamental plants, or their parts, are decorative, showy and attractive and are used for both beauty and function; they may be flowering or non-flowering.

en.text: Ornamental horticulture started recently in Ethiopia but is growing and is now one of the country's top exports. Opportunities include a suitable climate, ample land, cheap labour and water, nearness to Middle East and European markets, a growing domestic market and government incentives. It earns foreign currency, diversifies products, creates jobs, encourages supportive industries and promotes investment. Main crops include roses, poinsettia, geranium, chrysanthemum, lilies, carnation, gypsophila, statice, hypericum and freesia.
